drivers.variant_notes: The 1980 production ROM set (U1 819-08_1.716, U2 819-07_2.716, U6 720-40_6.732, sound 819-09_4.716) and the reference for this definition: GEN_BY35, seven-digit displays (dispBy7), FLIP_SW(FLIP_L), lampCol 0, sound board SNDBRD_BY51.

A 2004 Bally/Oliver free-play ROM (rev. 1) for the production hardware, replacing U2 and U6 with frnt2732.u2 and 7406fn.u6. Its info.txt enables free play when option switches S25 and S26 are both on, which on the production ROM set the maximum credits to 40. Its retained solenoid test fires the same thirteen outputs in the same order and publishes the same sixty lamps as the production set.

A 2011 patch of the production U6 (720-40_6g.732) for the same hardware. PinMAME's source quotes the patch, and applying it to the retained production U6 gives the SHA-1 PinMAME lists; the new code sets the U11 PIA port B bit that PinMAME publishes as output 17, closing the gate when a game starts or a player is added. The authorized ROM library holds no frontieg set, so it was not run.

Public 81 is column 11, bit 0 of PinMAME's generic flipper column (core_swSeq2m), which core.h names CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT: the lower-right flipper's end-of-stroke position. core_updateSw simulates that contact only for a driver declaring FLIP_EOS; Frontier's declares FLIP_SW(FLIP_L) only, so its flipper mask leaves the bit alone and the ROM never reads column 11. The VPinMAME Bally library calls the same address swURFlip, an upper-right flipper button, and writes it from the right flipper key whenever the table leaves its upper flipper solenoid number non-zero. core.vbs sets that number by default and zeroes it only through NoUpperLeftFlipper and NoUpperRightFlipper. The known-working script calls both, so it never writes the position; the retained table's embedded script lacks those calls and defines neither cSingleLFlip nor cSingleRFlip, so its flipper keys can write it as well. Either way nothing on this driver reads it, and holding it in play changed no output. Frontier has no upper flipper and nothing is fitted behind it.

Public 82 is the right cabinet flipper button. Frontier's buttons are not in the switch matrix: the plug-connector sheet wires them to the solenoid driver (A3J2-1 "R. FLIP. SW.", wire 10) so each switches its side's flipper coil through the K1 flipper-enable relay. The driver declares FLIP_SW(FLIP_L) without FLIP_SOL, so PinMAME reads this position of its own flipper column and raises the right flipper output 46 while the button is held and the relay (19) is up; the ROM never reads it. In play, holding 82 raised 46, and after a tilt it raised nothing.

mechanisms.behavior: Frontier is a one-ball game with no trough: the ball drains into the outhole below the flippers, closing switch 8, and the outhole kicker (public 7) serves it to the shooter alley, where the player launches it with the plunger. The ROM adds the bonus when the ball enters the outhole and fires both drop-target resets (8, 9) with the kick; a credit with the ball in the outhole starts the game, kicks the ball, fires both resets and the saucer kicker (10) in the same step.
mechanisms.label: Outhole and shooter feed

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets standing one behind the other along the left orbit, the 1st (switch 23) at the front to the 3rd (switch 21) at the rear, with the grizzly stand-up target (switch 24) beyond them at the end of the orbit; the ball reaches each only once the ones in front of it are down. The manual says any of them opens the gate; the first lights the spinner for 1,000, the second the Frontier 2X, the third the Frontier 3X and the grizzly target's values, and the grizzly target the Frontier 4X and 30,000. Completing the bank does not reset it: the ROM fires the shared reset coil (public 8) at power-on, at game start and at each drain.
mechanisms.label: Three in-line drop targets and the grizzly target

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets on the right side, bottom (switch 33), middle (34) and top (35), each scoring 500. Knocking all three down makes the ROM fire the shared reset coil (public 9) at once and steps the award: the Den of Predators 2X, then 3X, then 4X with the drop-target special lite, then a replay each time (manual). The outlane specials light with the second completion (option S14 on) or the third (S14 off). The ROM also fires the reset at power-on, at game start and at each drain.
mechanisms.label: Right-side three-bank drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: A saucer at the lower end of the upper-right lane. It collects the Frontier bonus (multiplied by any lit Frontier multiplier, per the manual) and the ROM kicks the ball out (public 10) straight up the lane, past the star rollover (25) and through the gate into the arch, as the manual's eject-saucer drawing shows.
mechanisms.label: Saucer

mechanisms.behavior: A gate at the top of the upper-right lane, where it meets the arch. The ROM holds its coil (public 17, a continuous output) on to open it: in play from the first in-line target until the ball rolled over the saucer rollover (25), or until the drain. Option S24 keeps an open gate for the next ball. On the production ROM adding a player leaves it open; the frontieg Gate Fix ROM closes it then. The known-working table models it as an invisible one-way gate held open while 17 is on.
mechanisms.label: Saucer lane gate

mechanisms.behavior: Two bumpers in the upper middle (left and right) and one below them in the centre. Each skirt switch makes the ROM fire its own coil: 40 fires 11, 39 fires 12 and 38 fires 13. The A, B and C lanes and their targets light the left, bottom and right bumper lamps (10, 26, 42), which the manual says score 1,000.
mechanisms.label: Three thumper bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: The pair above the flippers: switch 37 makes the ROM fire the left slingshot (14) and switch 36 the right (15).
mechanisms.label: Two slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: A spinner right of centre below the saucer lane whose switch closes once per rotation: 10 a closure, or 1,000 once the first in-line target has lit the spinner lamp (40).
mechanisms.label: Spinner

mechanisms.behavior: Two flippers, each fired by its cabinet button. The K1 relay (public 19) switches the flipper circuits: it is raised from game start to game over and dropped by a tilt.
mechanisms.label: Two flippers

PinMAME's synthetic right flipper state beside 46, not a second coil and not a measured power winding. Frontier's flipper coils are hard-wired, so the driver declares FLIP_SW(FLIP_L) without FLIP_SOL and core_updateSw fabricates the right pair 45/46 (CORE_LRFLIPSOLBITS; core.h names 45 sLRFlipPow and 46 sLRFlip) from the right button (82) while the K1 flipper-enable relay (19) is up: both rise together, stay asserted for the whole closure and fall together, so 45 carries the same state as 46. The BY35 controller profile declares it as meaningful duplicate state. In play, holding 82 raised 45 with 46, and the tilt, which dropped the relay, dropped 45 with 46. The known-working script binds nothing to it.

PinMAME publishes the generic lower-right flipper output 46 while the right button (82) is held with the relay up, together with its duplicate state 45, which has its own virtual record. The known-working script drives RightFlipper from 46.
